ety.text: Borrowed from Italian ombrella (“parasol, sunshade”), from Late Latin umbrella (influenced by umbra (“shadow, shade”)), from Latin umbella, from umbra + -la (diminutive suffix).

senses.d: A cloth-covered frame used for protection against rain or sun.
ex: Quick, grab that umbrella before you get rained on!
The fighters provide a defensive air umbrella over the battle group.

senses.d: Anything that provides similar overarching coverage of a range of concepts, purposes, groups, etc.
ex: The test facility was established under the umbrella of the company's quality program.

senses.d: A strategy in which five players in the offensive zone form an umbrella-shaped formation around the opposition's goal net.
The main body of a jellyfish, excluding the tentacles.
ex: Jellyfish are composed of more than 90% water and most of their umbrella mass is made up of gelatinous material.

senses.d: An umbrella-shaped reflector with a white or silvery inner surface, used to diffuse a nearby light.
ex: Using umbrellas for shooting a wedding party is ok, but not necessary.

senses.d: To cover or protect, as if by an umbrella.
ex: Huge pine and eucalyptus umbrellaed the grounds, airconditioning the morning.

senses.d: To form the dome shape of an open umbrella.
ex: Bright yellow gowns fit them tightly and umbrellaed from their waist to just below the knees.

ety.text: Borrowed from Italian ombrello, ombrella, from Late Latin umbrella, or formed from ombre + -elle, based on Latin umbella (whence French ombelle was borrowed), from umbra (“shade”). See ombre.
Verb-object compound, composed of para (“to protect; to block”) + pioggia (“rain”). Calque of French parapluie. Compare Sicilian paracqua.
Verb-object compound, composed of para (“to stop”) + aguas (“water(s)”).
